summary: Balloon-fed global weather observations, forecasts, benchmarks, and APIs.
editor_note: Live global observations make this weather stack more defensible than a forecast model trained only on public archives. Long-duration balloons feed WeatherMesh, while the public API, 10-minute refresh cadence, and live benchmark expose a product surface buyers can inspect. Unlike conventional numerical forecasts that may take hours, its model produces results in seconds. The unanswered question is whether company-run accuracy benchmarks predict customer outcomes across rare extremes.

product_evidence.claim: WindBorne combines observations from its Atlas long-duration balloon constellation with WeatherMesh, a transformer-based global forecast model.
The company exposes forecast access through public API documentation and publishes a live benchmark surface with a ten-minute refresh cadence.

market_context.primary_user: Weather-sensitive operators, insurers, energy teams, and forecasters that need frequently refreshed global observations and machine-readable predictions.
market_context.differentiation: A proprietary balloon observation network feeds a fast forecast model, while public API documentation and live benchmarks make the output inspectable.
market_context.why_now: The August 2026 Series B follows broader commercial interest in AI weather models and funds an observation network that can supply data unavailable in public archives.

risks.claim: Whether the company-run benchmark advantage predicts operational value during rare extreme events can be tested through independent, event-level customer results.
risks.basis: The public benchmarks improve inspectability, but the company controls both the forecast product and the displayed comparison surface.
